summary: A primary navigation destination. Renders an <a> when given `href`, a <button> otherwise.
useWhen: building a header nav bar, a sidebar or a section switcher
an item opens a menu rather than navigating — pass `showChevron` and no `href`

useInstead.when: the link sits inside body copy or a content block
it is a row in a dropdown list rather than a top-level destination

icon.note: leading icon; omit its `label` — the item's text names it

a11y.role: link when `href` is set, button when it is not
guarantees: hover state comes from React Aria's pointer-aware `useHover`, so a tap does not stay hovered until the next tap elsewhere
the focus ring shows for keyboard navigation only
the CSS keeps its own `:hover` / `:focus-visible` rules, so the styling survives without React
requires: an accessible name — `children`, or `aria-label` on an icon-only item
notes: NavItem is one item, not the landmark. Wrap the set in a <nav> with its own accessible name.

antiPatterns.dont: `showChevron` on a plain link that navigates
antiPatterns.why: the chevron promises a menu; nothing opens

antiPatterns.dont: marking the current page with colour only
antiPatterns.why: a screen-reader user is otherwise never told where they are
